title: Speed: distillation, caching, compile, fewer steps
hook: Four levers, four different mechanisms. Count what each one saves, and what it asks in return.

verified.claim: When CFG is 1 the second conditioning is dropped, unless disable_cfg1_optimization is set.
EasyCache and LazyCache are core nodes marked experimental. Their defaults are reuse threshold 0.2 and a window of 0.15 to 0.95.
TorchCompileModel is an experimental node with inductor and cudagraphs backends. It is not a setting.
The node cache keys on class, inputs and ancestors, and caches whole node results.
A prefix cache keeps keys and values for one model family's prefix, such as prompt and references.
Progressive distillation trains a student to match two teacher steps with one. Consistency models learn to map any point on a trajectory to its start.
Error and call counts in the Lab come from a run here on a toy ODE.

unchecked: We timed none of these levers in this lesson. The lab counts calls, and speed gains depend on the model and the card.
We did not test whether torch.compile helps on any model, or what its first-run cost is here. The advice to time the second run is general.
Quality changes from a cache or a distilled model are for your eyes. The toy ODE's error is not a picture.
